{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Fix the revenue column: remove commas and convert to float
# First, check if any revenue values are actually '999999.99' or similar
print("Revenue values:", df['revenue'].unique()[:10])

# Replace commas in revenue and convert to float
df['revenue'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Now check again for QA orders (999999.99) and negative values
qa_count = (df['revenue'] == 999999.99).sum()
print("Number of QA orders (revenue == 999999.99):", qa_count)

negative_revenue_count = (df['revenue'] < 0).sum()
print("Number of negative revenue values:", negative_revenue_count)

# Check if there are any refunded orders
refunded_count = (df['status'] == 'refunded').sum()
print("Number of refunded orders:", refunded_count)

# Now filter for NEW customers reached by PAID SEARCH
filtered = df[
    (df['customer_segment'] == 'new') &
    (df['channel'] == 'paid_search')
]

print("Filtered data shape:", filtered.shape)

# Check if any of these filtered rows are refunded or QA
print("QA orders in filtered group:", (filtered['revenue'] == 999999.99).sum())
print("Refunded orders in filtered group:", (filtered['status'] == 'refunded').sum())

# Now, compute the conversion fraction: completed / total
# Only count completed orders for conversion
completed_count = (filtered['status'] == 'completed').sum()
total_count = len(filtered)
conversion_fraction = completed_count / total_count

print(f"Completed: {completed_count}")
print(f"Total: {total_count}")
print(f"Conversion fraction: {conversion_fraction}")

# Final check: ensure no QA or refunded orders are in the count
# We already checked above — but double-check
assert (filtered['revenue'] == 999999.99).sum() == 0, "QA orders found in filtered group"
assert (filtered['status'] == 'refunded').sum() == 0, "Refunded orders found in filtered group"

# Output the fraction as a float between 0 and 1
conversion_fraction"}
